description: AeroBrain STE project dictionary. Machine-readable twin of docs/STE_STYLE_GUIDE.md. Not the official ASD-STE100 dictionary. basis: sheet = owner reference sheet, ste = widely documented STE substitution, project = project decision that follows the STE rule of one word for one meaning.

achieve.note: GET a result. Do not use ACHIEVE.

activate.note: TURN ON a switch. START a process.

actually.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

adjacent.note: NEXT TO is the approved phrase.

assure.note: Same meaning as ENSURE. Use MAKE SURE.

basically.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

begin.note: One word for one meaning: START.

close.note: CLOSE is approved only as a verb (to close a valve). As an adjective, use NEAR.

configure.note: SET an option. Use `config` for the name of the file.

could.note: Use CAN. For a past event, use the simple past.

deactivate.note: TURN OFF is the approved phrase.

determine.note: FIND a value. DECIDE a choice.

disable.note: Use TURN OFF for a switch or a flag.

due to.note: BECAUSE OF is the approved phrase.

easily.note: Vague. State the real condition or delete the word.

enable.note: Use TURN ON for a switch or a flag. ENABLE is jargon.

ensure.note: MAKE SURE is the approved phrase for this meaning.

essentially.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

etc.note: Give the full list, or say what the other items are.

etc..note: Give the full list, or say what the other items are.

exceed.note: Say what is more than what.

execute.note: RUN a program, script or command.

fall back.note: Write what the system uses instead.

however.note: Use BUT or start a new sentence.

incorporate.note: PUT IN is the approved phrase.

initialise.note: START a program. SET a first value.

initialize.note: START a program. SET a first value.

invoke.note: RUN a program or command. START a service.

launch.note: Use START for a process. For a drone, use TAKE OFF.

maintain.note: KEEP a state. DO MAINTENANCE ON equipment.

may.note: CAN shows a possibility. MAY is not approved.

multiple.note: MANY is the approved word. Use `multi-source` as a technical name.

obviously.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

of course.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

once.note: ONCE means one time only. Use AFTER or WHEN for time order.

persist.note: SAVE data to disk. KEEP a value.

prohibit.note: Write the prohibition as a command: Do not ...

provide.note: GIVE or SUPPLY. For a feature, use HAVE.

quite.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

really.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

require.note: NEED is the approved word. Write: The job needs 8 GB.

reside.note: Write: The file is in ... Do not use RESIDE.

shall.note: MUST shows a rule. WILL shows the future.

should.note: MUST shows a rule. For advice, write an imperative or state the condition.

simply.note: Filler word. It adds no information. Delete it.

specify.note: GIVE a value. SET an option.

supplement.note: ADD TO is the approved phrase.

trigger.note: START a process. CAUSE an effect.

validate.note: Same decision as VERIFY. A gate that checks a rule is a CHECK.

verify.note: Use MAKE SURE when you state the result you expect. Use CHECK when you name the action (check the log). VERIFY has more than one meaning.

via.note: THROUGH a path. WITH a tool.

about.meaning: Near to a number. Also: on the subject of.

after.example: After the job ends, check the log.

because of.example: The job stops because of an error.

before.example: Before you start, stop the worker.

check.meaning: Look at something to see its state.

fill.example: Fill the disk with the data.

find.meaning: Get a value by a search.
find.example: Find the job in the log.

help.example: The log helps you find the error.

if.example: If the PC is off, wake it.

make sure.meaning: Do an action or a check so that the result is certain.
make sure.example: Make sure that the worker is idle.

many.example: Many jobs are in the queue.

near.example: Do not fly near a building.

show.example: The page shows the job state.

so.example: The key is wrong, so the request fails.

test.meaning: Run a check on a function.

then.example: Stop the worker. Then restart the web.

to.meaning: For the purpose of (replaces `in order to`).

try.meaning: Do an action that can fail.

turn off.meaning: Make a switch or a flag not active.

turn on.meaning: Make a switch or a flag active.

use.meaning: Do work with a tool or a value.

when.example: When the job ends, the worker takes the next one.

will.example: The worker will start the next job.

Software components.AeroBrain: The name of this project and of its web application.
Software components.Flightverse: The 3D flight and game mode of the web application.
Software components.Splat Lab: The web page where you edit and clean a splat.
Software components.SuperSplat: The splat editor that the project hosts. The project keeps its own fork.
Software components.worker: The one background process that takes jobs from the queue and runs them.
Software components.web origin: The Python web server on 127.0.0.1:8790. It serves the web files, the APIs and the video.
Software components.watchdog: The LaunchAgent that checks the web, the worker and the tunnel and starts them again.
Software components.tunnel: The Cloudflare Tunnel process (`cloudflared`) that connects the web origin to the Internet.
Software components.LaunchAgent: A macOS background service that `launchd` starts for one user.
Software components.manifest: The JSON file or index that lists the clips, scenes and models in the vault.
Software components.vault: The folder `/Volumes/SSD/drone-vault` that holds all drone data.
Software components.clip: One video recording with its SRT file.
Software components.scene: A 3D site with one or more versions.
Software components.scene version: One reconstruction of a scene, for example `recon_<hash>`.
Software components.job: One unit of work in the queue, for example an ODM job or a splat job.
Software components.queue: The list of jobs in `jobs.db`. The worker takes one job at a time.
Software components.jobs.db: The SQLite file that stores the job queue.
Software components.gate: An automatic check that a result must pass before the next step starts.
Software components.preflight: A set of checks that run before a restart or a publish.
Software components.sidecar: A file next to another file, for example a `.gz` file next to a web asset.
Software components.proxy: A small, low-resolution copy of a video.
Software components.edge Worker: The Cloudflare Worker in `edge/` that signs the session cookie for the origin.
Software components.SQLite: The file database that the project uses.
Software components.jobs console: The page 3D, Trabajos in the web application.
Software components.auto-clean: The Splat Lab function that removes floaters from a splat.
Software components.floater: A stray splat or point that floats in the air and does not belong to the scene.

3D and capture.splat: A 3D model that is made of many Gaussian blobs. The file types are `.ply`, `.splat` and `.ksplat`.
3D and capture.Gaussian splat: The full name of a splat.
3D and capture.mesh: A 3D surface that is made of triangles.
3D and capture.DSM: Digital Surface Model. A raster of the height of the ground and of all objects on it.
3D and capture.DTM: Digital Terrain Model. A raster of the height of the bare ground.
3D and capture.ortho: The orthophoto. A top view image of the site with no perspective distortion.
3D and capture.point cloud: A set of 3D points that ODM makes from the photos.
3D and capture.collider: A simple shape that the game uses to find hits between the drone and the world.
3D and capture.heightmap: A raster image where each pixel is a height.
3D and capture.GCP: Ground Control Point. A target with known coordinates.
3D and capture.EXIF: The metadata in a photo file, for example the GPS position.
3D and capture.SRT: The subtitle file that a DJI drone writes next to a video. It holds the GPS track.
3D and capture.nadir: Straight down. A nadir photo has the camera at -90 degrees.
3D and capture.oblique: At an angle. An oblique photo has the camera not straight down.
3D and capture.lawnmower: A flight pattern of parallel straight lines.
3D and capture.gimbal: The part that holds and turns the camera.
3D and capture.doming: A model error where flat ground bends like a bowl.
3D and capture.overlap: The share of one photo that other photos also show.
3D and capture.LOD: Level Of Detail. A simpler version of a model for far views.
3D and capture.rolling shutter: A camera effect. The sensor reads the image line by line, so fast motion bends straight lines.

Tools and platforms.ODM: OpenDroneMap. The photogrammetry program that makes the point cloud, the DSM and the ortho.
Tools and platforms.OpenMVS: The dense reconstruction part of ODM.
Tools and platforms.COLMAP: A structure-from-motion program and file format.
Tools and platforms.gsplat: The CUDA library that trains a splat.
Tools and platforms.OpenSplat: The older splat trainer that ran on the Mac.
Tools and platforms.OrbStack: The macOS program that runs Docker containers.
Tools and platforms.WoL: Wake-on-LAN. A network packet that wakes a sleeping computer.
Tools and platforms.Cloudflare: The company and the network service that carries the public traffic.
Tools and platforms.Python: The programming language of the pipeline.
Tools and platforms.HMAC: A signature method with a shared key.
Tools and platforms.CSRF: Cross-site request forgery. An attack that the project blocks.
Tools and platforms.endpoint: One URL path of the API.
Tools and platforms.Markdown: The text format of the docs.
Tools and platforms.Fetch Metadata: A web standard. The browser adds Sec-Fetch headers to a request. The headers show where the request comes from.
Tools and platforms.Pixel Streaming: A product of Unreal Engine. It sends the rendered image of an Unreal application from a server GPU to a web browser.

Hardware and drones.RTX 4060 Ti: The NVIDIA GPU in the PC. It has 8 GB of memory.
Hardware and drones.Mac Mini M4: The Mac that runs the web, the worker and the tunnel.
Hardware and drones.the PC: The Windows computer with the GPU. You reach it with `ssh pc`.
Hardware and drones.DJI Flip: A small DJI camera drone. It flies by hand only.
Hardware and drones.DJI Neo 2: A small DJI camera drone. It has a wide lens and flies by hand only.
Hardware and drones.SD card: The memory card of the drone.
Hardware and drones.RPAS: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System. A drone.
Hardware and drones.VLOS: Visual Line Of Sight. The pilot sees the drone with the eyes.

Files, paths and products.ALERT: The file `~/Library/Logs/AeroBrain/ALERT`. It exists only while a check fails.
Files, paths and products.ops_status.py: The script that prints the PASS or FAIL status of the system.
Files, paths and products.safe_restart.sh: The script that restarts a service in a safe way.
Files, paths and products.run_all_tests.py: The script that runs all the test suites.
Files, paths and products.gcp_list.txt: The ground control point file for ODM.
Files, paths and products.CLAUDE.md: The file of pitfalls for coding agents.
Files, paths and products.AGENTS.md: The file of access and acceptance rules for coding agents.

Release and deploy.deploy: Put a new version of the code on a live service.
Release and deploy.publish: Make a result visible in the web application. It also means: send a file to the vault.
Release and deploy.bump: Increase a version number. For example `bump_web_version.py` increases `?v=N`.
Release and deploy.rebake: Make a baked file again, for example a collision file.
Release and deploy.bake: Calculate a result once and save it in a file.
Release and deploy.rebuild: Build a program or an index again from its sources.
Release and deploy.generate: Make a file or data with a program.
Release and deploy.promote: Make a scene version the active version.
Release and deploy.roll back: Go back to the last good version.

Version control.commit: Save a set of changes in the Git history.
Version control.push: Send Git commits to the remote on GitHub.
Version control.pull: Get Git commits from the remote.
Version control.merge: Join two Git branches, or join the data of two sources.
Version control.tag: Put a label on a Git commit.

Process control.restart: Stop a service and start it again.
Process control.kickstart: Start a LaunchAgent now with `launchctl kickstart`.
Process control.kill: Stop a process at once with a signal.
Process control.cancel: Stop a job before it is finished.
Process control.enqueue: Put a job in the queue.
Process control.re-enqueue: Put a job in the queue again.
Process control.rerun: Run a job or a command again.
Process control.probe: Send a small test request to see if a service answers.
Process control.poll: Ask a service for its state again and again.
Process control.tail: Show the last lines of a log file.
Process control.drain: Take all the jobs out of a queue and run them.
Process control.stage: Copy files to a temporary place before a job.
Process control.wake: Wake a sleeping computer with WoL.

Data and files.ingest: Copy files from the SD card into the vault and register them.
Data and files.extract: Take frames or files out of a video or an archive.
Data and files.convert: Change a file from one format to another.
Data and files.export: Write data in a file format for use in another tool.
Data and files.import: Read data from another tool or format.
Data and files.upload: Send a file from the browser or the Mac to a server.
Data and files.download: Get a file from a server.
Data and files.parse: Read a text file and split it into its parts.
Data and files.purge: Delete files for good to free disk space.
Data and files.delete: Remove a file or a record.
Data and files.trash: Move a file to the trash folder. It is not deleted.
Data and files.sync: Make two copies of data the same.
Data and files.rotate: Replace a key or a log file with a new one.
Data and files.crop: Cut a part out of a model or an image.
Data and files.gzip: Compress a file with the gzip program.
Data and files.register: Add an item to a list or an index.

3D and compute.render: Draw an image from a 3D model.
3D and compute.train: Run an optimizer that makes a splat from photos.
3D and compute.align: Move a model so that it fits a reference.
3D and compute.clean: Remove floaters and noise from a splat.
3D and compute.filter: Remove points or data that do not pass a rule.
3D and compute.sample: Take a part of the data for a test.
3D and compute.bundle: Join many files into one file.
3D and compute.downsample: Make a copy of the data with fewer points.

Software testing.lint: Run a program that checks the style of files.
Software testing.gate: Stop a step until a check passes.
Software testing.stress: Run a test with a high load.
Software testing.mock: Replace a real part with a fake part in a test.
